**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – first 7 days, first class experience, induction checklist, liability waivers, payment setup, goal-setting call. *Why critical: determines retention trajectory; every delay compounds churn risk.*
- **Member Pause/Cancellation/Churn** – pause request workflow, billing pause, re-engagement trigger points, exit interview capture, win-back sequences. *Why critical: predictable revenue leakage; no documented decision tree means ad-hoc handling.*
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – progression from hire through mastery (probation → Level 1 → Level 2 → Lead Coach); certification, observation schedules, skill gaps, promotion criteria. *Why critical: coach quality degrades without structured growth; inconsistent class experience.*
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – observation framework (cuing, pacing, class energy, member safety, music/timing, corrections), audit frequency (e.g. quarterly per coach), scoring, feedback loop. *Why critical: 28 client SOPs but no mechanism to verify coaches actually deliver them.*
- **Member Data Privacy & GDPR** – data collection consent flows, retention/deletion timelines, DPA compliance for contact/payment data, member data access requests, breach protocol. *Why critical: legal exposure; especially acute with female-only member base and biometric/health data.*
- **Referral Programme** – eligibility, reward trigger, payout mechanism (credit vs. cash), tracking in CRM, fraud prevention. *Why critical: cheapest acquisition channel; undefined = no growth lever.*

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your coaches — they're your source of truth**
Run a 30-min workshop with your coaching team. Ask: "What do we actually sell?" (Not what you think you sell — what they deliver daily). Capture every service variant they currently mention: group classes, 1-on-1 packages, nutrition add-ons, form checks, progress tracking. This reveals what's *already* generating value.

**2. Price by outcome, not time**
Don't list "60-min session = £40." Instead: "6-week strength foundation package (2x weekly + form videos) = £X." Women buy transformation, not minutes. Test pricing on your most recent members — ask what they'd pay for the exact outcome they got. Use that data.

**3. Create two separate menus — literally different documents**
**Coach menu:** Lists every service with profit margins, time commitment, and upsell triggers (e.g., "When member hits 4 weeks, mention nutrition audit"). **Member menu:** Clean, benefit-focused, no jargon. Show what problem each service solves ("Nutrition audit: Stop guessing what actually works for *your* body").

**4. Hardcode this into your booking system TODAY**
Don't create a PDF and file it. Build it into your gym's booking/CRM system so coaches see the full menu when a member books. Friction kills upsells — make it frictionless for them to suggest the right next step.

**5. Test it for 2 weeks with one coach**
Pick your most adaptable coach. Have her use the new menu structure with 10 members. Track which services actually convert and which

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO REPORT

## REVENUE — CRITICAL ISSUE: MEMBER QUALITY COLLAPSING

**Last 3 months (Aug–Oct): £16,160 → £22,016 → £17,783. Member count up 20 (153→173), revenue DOWN £4,233 month-on-month. Rev/member crashed from £136 (Sep) to £103 (Oct). This is your biggest red flag.**

- **Pricing audit now.** You're onboarding at lower price points or losing higher-tier members to churn. Oct churn 3.9% is good, but Aug–Sep average 5.9% suggests recent joiners are weaker-quality. Run cohort analysis: what price did Sep joiners pay vs Aug? Implement tiered pricing for new members (entry £35/month, standard £45, premium £60 with classes/PT bundle). Target Rev/member back to £130+ by December.

- **Upsell PT & class bundles to existing base.** 173 active members at £103 per head is leaving £4,500+/month on table. Identify 30–40 mid-tenure members (3–6 months in) for one-to-one PT trial offer (£25 intro, bundle at £15/class on top of membership). Projected uptake 20%+ = £1,200+ incremental monthly.

- **Halt the churn bleeding in Sep.** May 12.8% churn spike signals either a pricing change, class schedule disruption, or cohort quality issue around that intake. Cross-check: did you run a discount offer in Jul? Were there facility complaints Sep–Oct? Fix root cause before it repeats.

---

## EXPENSES — SCALE WORKING, BUT STAFFING RISK LOOMS

- **You've grown 53 members (+44%) since March without proportional opex growth** (assumed: rent/utilities locked post-relocation, headcount stable). This is healthy margin leverage. **Do not hire a second full-time staff member until Oct revenue repeats for 2 consecutive months.** Current model (likely 1 FT manager + PT instructors on class fees?) is efficient. Once you hit £20k+ recurring, add PT coordinator 12–15 hrs/week, outsourced.

- **Supplier cost review: check card processing fees.** GoCardless + Stripe on £16–22k/month at standard UK rates = £400–550/month drag (2.4–2.8%). Negotiate: if >2.5%, move GoCardless recurring to Stripe API direct
